title: Rich People Share Biggest Money Mistakes They Made in Their 20s — 'The Problem Wasn't Earning It, It Was Keeping It'
detail:
Rich People Share Biggest Money Mistakes They Made in Their 20s — 'The Problem Wasn't Earning It, It Was Keeping It'
Image via Shutterstock
Casey B. Renner
Wed, September 16, 2026 at 10:45 AM EDT 7 min read
RDDT

Making more money sounds like the obvious way to get ahead in your 20s. But earning it and actually building wealth with it can be two very different things.

A user asked wealthy people what they wished they had started earlier and what advice they would give someone in their 20s in a post on Reddit's r/wealth community.

"The problem wasn't earning it, it was keeping it," a commenter wrote.

Don't Miss:

Warren Buffett once said, "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die." Here's how you can earn passive income with just $100.

AI Needs More Power Than The Grid Can Easily Provide. This Startup Is Taking A Different Approach To Energy Storage.

A Higher Income Could Disappear Into A Better Lifestyle

That commenter said they spent their 20s trying to make as much money as possible, but some of it went toward bigger houses, nicer cars, private jets and other upgrades. Real estate and businesses eventually made them wealthy, yet they still wished they had put more into the stock market along the way.

"Whether that's real estate, individual stocks, or ETFs doesn't matter nearly as much as consistently adding to them," they wrote.

Another commenter had come to a similar conclusion after landing a well-paying job.

"Upgrading my lifestyle didn't make me happier, it just raised my standards," the person wrote. Instead, they said they now keep things that still work and put most of their excess income into investments, hoping to eventually cut back to part-time work and retire early.

Starting Earlier Left More Room For Time To Work

A commenter in their 30s said they bought their first stock and cryptocurrency at 21, and some of those investments later rose more than 50 times in value.

"People that started even a few years later, now have to do a lot of catch up to get there," they wrote.

Trending: There's More Than One Way To Put Cash To Work. Some Accredited Investors Are Looking Beyond Savings Accounts.

But another commenter didn't think those early years should be spent only saving and investing.

"Save money… the compounding effects (aka rule of 72) are amazing!" the person wrote. But they didn't suggest spending an entire 20s preparing for some distant future. The same commenter urged younger people to travel, go on adventures and try new things, adding that "those experiences in your 20s are compounders too!"

title: My Dad Is 65 and Turned $75K Into $1M, but It’s in One Stock and His Entire Retirement. He’s Asking Me If He Should Sell Everything?

Turning $75,000 into $1 million sounds like a straight-up brag — the kind of investing win that makes a person feel like they cracked the code. But when that $1 million is sitting almost entirely in one stock, the brag starts looking a lot more complicated.

That's the situation a Reddit user brought to the r/investingforbeginners community while asking for advice about his father. Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ:STX) was essentially his dad's entire retirement portfolio, and at 65, he was starting to wonder whether it was finally time to cash out.

"My father's $75,000 dollar investment is now valued at $1,000,000 but it's all in one stock," the poster wrote.

Don't Miss:

If You Have $1M+, Your Wealth May Need More Than A Traditional Advisor. See What A Family Office Approach Looks Like.

He Thought He Needed $88K To Invest In Real Estate. Then He Found A Way To Start With $100.

His father had accumulated 1,340 shares of Seagate after purchasing stock while working for the company. His cost basis was $55.32 per share. After the stock's recent run-up, he reached out to his son to ask whether he should sell everything.

Before his son could get back to him, his father sold 75 shares at $650.

The remaining money was still almost entirely tied to Seagate. There was nothing in retirement accounts, he carried minimal debt and was still earning $48,000 a year. His wife didn't work and was a few years younger.

"I'm terrified this is their only chance at retirement," the poster wrote.

One Stock, One Retirement

The son initially thought his father could hold the position and sell only what he needed each year while taking advantage of long-term capital-gains tax treatment.

He also floated a more complicated strategy involving covered calls and using the premiums to build a diversified portfolio. He had been using the strategy with his own investments.

Trending: AI Needs More Power Than The Grid Can Easily Provide. This Startup Is Taking A Different Approach To Energy Storage.

Reddit commenters weren't exactly enthusiastic.

One of the most popular responses kept it simple:

"I don't typically advocate taking profits but holy shit, take the profit and diversify."

Another commenter suggested selling at least half the position.

Others focused on the bigger issue: concentration risk.

The problem isn't necessarily that Seagate is a bad company. It's that retirement money has a very different job than money being invested for long-term growth.

Q2 Social Networking Earnings: Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) Earns Top Marks

Earnings results often indicate what direction a company will take in the months ahead. With Q2 behind us, let's have a look at Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) and its peers.

Businesses must meet their customers where they are, which over the past decade has come to mean on social networks. In 2020, users spent over 2.5 hours a day on social networks, a figure that has increased every year since measurement began. As a result, businesses continue to shift their advertising and marketing dollars online.

The 5 social networking stocks we track reported a strong Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 4% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 1.1% above.

While some social networking stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 3.4% since the latest earnings results.

Best Q2: Reddit (NYSE:RDDT)

Founded in 2005 by two University of Virginia roommates, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) facilitates user-generated content across niche communities (called subreddits) that discuss anything from stocks to dating and memes.

Reddit reported revenues of $804.9 million, up 61.1% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 9.9%. Overall, it was a stunning quarter for the company with a solid beat of analysts' EBITDA estimates and EBITDA guidance for next quarter exceeding analysts' expectations.

"In an increasingly automated web, the value of real human perspective has never been higher. Reddit's commercial momentum reflects that," said Steve Huffman, Founder and CEO of Reddit.

Reddit Total Revenue

Reddit pulled off the biggest analyst estimate beat, highest guidance raise, and fastest revenue growth in the group. The company reported 53.2 million daily active users, up 5.8% year on year. Investor expectations, however, were likely higher than Wall Street's published projections, leaving some wishing for even better results (analysts' consensus estimates are those published by big banks and advisory firms, not the investors who make buy and sell decisions). The stock is down 9.1% since reporting and currently trades at $161.83.

Read why we think that Reddit is one of the best social networking stocks, our full report is free.

Snap (NYSE:SNAP)

Founded by Stanford University students Evan Spiegel, Reggie Brown, and Bobby Murphy, and originally called Picaboo, Snapchat (NYSE: SNAP) is an image centric social media network.

Snap reported revenues of $1.60 billion, up 18.9% year on year, outperforming analysts' expectations by 3.8%. The business had an exceptional quarter with a solid beat of analysts' EBITDA estimates.

title: Reddit Finally Gets a Breakout Catalyst. This Could Be Turning Point for the Beaten-Down Stock.
detail:
Reddit Finally Gets a Breakout Catalyst. This Could Be Turning Point for the Beaten-Down Stock.
Nauman Khan
Tue, September 15, 2026 at 11:05 AM EDT 4 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
A hand holding a phone with the Reddit logo_ Mamun_Sheikh via Shutterstock_

Reddit (RDDT) stock finally gave investors something to cheer about. Shares jumped about 6% on Sept. 10 after Piper Sandler data showed Reddit's user base grew 8% month over month in August. That marked the company's strongest monthly gain of 2026 and a sharp reversal from the roughly 2% decline in July.

The move also snapped a four-session losing streak. But there's still a major problem. Reddit shares remain down 30% in 2026 and down roughly 38% over the past year. The big question now is whether August marked the beginning of a real turnaround or just another short-lived bounce. Let's take a closer look.

August User Growth Could Change the Reddit Stock Story

The August data matters because user growth has become Reddit's biggest problem with investors.

Piper Sandler said Reddit's total audience growth accelerated to 18% year-over-year (YOY) in August, up from 12.8% in July. International growth was especially impressive, climbing 29.3% compared with 19% a month earlier. Meanwhile, U.S. users grew 5.2%.

The improvement came mainly from Reddit's Feed audience, offsetting a decline in Conversation users. That could be important for RDDT stock because Reddit relies heavily on traffic and user engagement to build its advertising business. For months, investors have worried about volatility in search referrals and whether Reddit can keep expanding without depending so heavily on Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google.

August offers an encouraging sign.

Piper Sandler also raised its Reddit advertising-spending forecast by 30 basis points after broader digital ad spending beat expectations. However, the firm expects September audience estimates to fall about 20% because Reddit changed its Ads Manager forecasting methodology. Piper Sandler described that as a one-time measurement reset rather than a deterioration in demand.

For Reddit stock, the key issue is whether the August acceleration will continue over the next few months.

Reddit's Q2 Results Show the Business Is Still Growing Fast

The latest quarterly numbers give the bulls plenty to work with. Reddit reported second-quarter revenue of $805 million on July 30, up 61% YOY. Advertising revenue climbed 64% to $762 million, while other revenue, including data licensing, rose 24% YOY to $43 million.

Investors looking for cheap stocks to buy before the end of 2026 don't have to look too far to find some great investments. There are many top stocks that can make for solid long-term growth investments that are trading at absurdly cheap valuations right now.

Three stocks that are trading at low earnings multiples and that have lots of growth still ahead are Novo Nordisk (NYSE:NVO), Intuit (NASDAQ:INTU), and Reddit (NYSE:RDDT). Here's why these can make for great growth stocks to buy right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Novo Nordisk

It's been a rough stretch for healthcare company Novo Nordisk, as it has declined about 23% in value over the past 12 months. Investors are questioning its ability to grow and compete alongside its rival, Eli Lilly. Novo was an early leader in the GLP-1 race with Ozempic and Wegovy, but now has lost more than a couple of steps.

The reason I'm not worried and remain invested in the stock, however, is that there are still ample growth opportunities ahead for Novo. A higher-dose version of Wegovy has shown that it can help people lose even more weight. And the company is still in the early innings of the launch of its weight loss pill, which obtained approval from regulators late last year.

Novo's sales have been underwhelming of late, and it has a new CEO working to turn things around. There's some uncertainty ahead, no doubt about that. But this is still an excellent healthcare company to invest in for the long haul. And its stock is trading at an absurdly low forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 13, which is based on analyst projections. It's absurdly cheap and practically a no-brainer buy at these levels.

Intuit

One of the worst stocks within the S&P 500 this year has been Intuit, the software company known for popular titles such as TurboTax and QuickBooks. Professionals rely on its software on a daily basis, but the threat that artificial intelligence (AI) will disrupt its business has weighed the stock down heavily -- it's crashed around 50% this year.

AI is a threat that I believe is a gross miscalculation when it comes to Intuit. Tax and accounting are not things I believe that consumers and business professionals are going to rely on AI for, as errors or hallucinations for these types of tasks can be extremely costly for users.

Reddit's international daily active uniques surged 28% and international revenue climbed 84%, pointing to significant untapped monetization potential abroad.

Meta held near flat while Snap gained 1% on improving ad conditions, offering investors steadier or higher-risk alternatives to Reddit's volatile growth story.

Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) stock is falling 4% to $156.49 in Tuesday morning trading, putting the social-media company under pressure despite Reddit's continued user growth. Reddit's latest quarterly results showed daily active uniques increased 18% year over year to 130.3 million, while weekly active uniques climbed 24% to 514.6 million.

stockcam / iStock Unreleased via Getty Images

The broader social-media group is showing a mixed picture, with Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock down 0.34% to $663.31 and Snap (NYSE:SNAP) stock rising 1% to $5.88. The Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) is up 2% to $44.90, while SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) is unchanged at $760.60.

Reddit's User Growth Remains A Bullish Signal

Reddit's 18% increase in daily active uniques gives the bullish case a meaningful foundation, particularly because Reddit also produced 61% year-over-year revenue growth to $805 million in the second quarter. Reddit's adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $343 million, while free cash flow reached $261 million.

Reddit's international audience is another encouraging point, with international daily active uniques increasing 28% year over year compared with 6% growth in the U.S. Reddit's international revenue also climbed 84%, suggesting that expanding usage outside the U.S. could provide additional monetization opportunities.

The Stock Still Faces A Higher Bar

Reddit stock's 4% decline suggests strong operating growth isn't automatically translating into positive trading momentum. Reddit stock can remain sensitive to expectations around future growth, advertising monetization and the durability of its AI-related data opportunities.
